05 /15.04.2024: I.A. No.3496 of 2024 This interlocutory application has been filed by the appellant,
praying therein to suspend the sentence and release him on bail during pendency of this appeal.
2. The appellant has been convicted and sentenced in connection with Sessions Trial Case No. 37 of 2021, for the offence under Section 376(1) of the IPC.
He has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 14 years & fine of Rs.1,00,000/- for the offence under Section 376(1) of the IPC.

3. Heard, the learned counsel for the appellant learned A.P.P. for the State and learned counsel for the informant and have gone through the impugned judgment, the evidence and the Trial Court Records.
4. Opportunity was given to the State and the informant to oppose the bail, which the both availed and opposed.
5. The victim who is admittedly a major stated that on 15.9.2020 this appellant called the victim and thereafter committed rape.
She also stated that the entire incident was videographed and thereafter this appellant used to blackmail and establish physical relationship.
Due to the physical relationship she became pregnant.
It has also been stated that this appellant assured that he will marry with her but he did not marry, rather some pills were given to her due to which miscarriage was caused.

It has been stated that father of the informant also went to the house of this appellant with marriage Md. Azad Iraki @ Md. Azad Eraqui vs State Of Jharkhand on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40464965/
1 proposal but the same was not accepted.

sentences.text: Thereafter FIR was lodged.
Incident had taken place on 15.9.2020 and complaint was lodged on 02.02.2021 which was sent under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C to the police station.
No FIR and complaint was lodged when the victim became pregnant and miscarriage had occurred at the instance of this appellant.
Parties are major and the appellant was on bail during trial.
Further we find that though there is allegation that this appellant used to tease the victim for considerable period of time, yet no complaint was lodged then.
6. Considering the aforesaid facts and the fact that there is no likelihood of this appeal being heard in near future, we are inclined to allow this interlocutory application.

Accordingly, upon suspending the sentence, the appellant above named is directed to be released on bail during the pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the District & Additional Sessions Judge-III, Godda in connection with Sessions Trial Case No. 37 of 2021 with a condition that appellant shall appear and mark his attendance before the Registrar, Civil Court, Godda once in every four months till the disposal of this appeal.
7. This interlocutory application is, accordingly, allowed.
